subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw support `agents.list[].compaction` and `agents.list[].contextPruning` as a public per-agent config contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 be the landing path?
rationale: The source-reproduced gap is real, but adding this config surface changes strict user-facing config, compaction model routing, and session-context semantics, which requires maintainer product intent before another automated fix path is safe.

options.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
options.body: Approve per-agent `compaction` and `contextPruning` with deep-merge semantics over defaults, then repair and prove the open implementation PR before merge.

options.title: Narrow to compaction model first
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` for provider/cost isolation now and defer broader compaction/pruning knobs to a later design issue.

options.title: Keep defaults-only behavior
options.body: Decline this config expansion and close or redirect the open implementation attempts, leaving users with global defaults or separate deployments.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the additive per-agent contract
recommendation.body: Approve per-agent `compaction` and `contextPruning` with deep-merge semantics over defaults, then repair and prove the open implementation PR before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history on the central agent-scope config helper path and current main config/schema work.
